summary: Iteration 8 — targeted infra/config smoke only (9 assertions requested). Created /app/backend/tests/test_iteration8_infra_smoke.py: 7 pytest tests, all PASSED. Verified (1) GET /api/health 200 status=healthy/database=healthy; (2)(3)(4) logins for patient@, doctor1@, admin@careflow.demo return 200, set httponly session_token cookie, and GET /api/auth/me returns the correct email/role via cookie (no password_hash/_id leakage); (5) GET /api/reports as admin returns 200 list; (6) admin multipart upload POST /api/reports/upload (minimal PDF) returns 200 and GET /api/reports/{id}/file returns 200 with byte-identical content and application/pdf; (7) unauthorized access — patient with no released report gets 404, non-uploader doctor2 gets 403, unauthenticated gets 401; (8) headless browser fetch of REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL/api/health from the frontend origin returned 200 healthy (landing page renders fine); (9) backend imports/starts cleanly with the _require_env helper (supervisor logs show 'Application startup complete', no import errors). Additionally reproduced the original bug scenario: running server.py with MONGO_URL/DB_NAME/AUTH_SECRET unset now raises RuntimeError with the actionable 'Copy backend/.env.example to backend/.env...' message instead of KeyError — fix confirmed. Test upload row + file were deleted after the run (verified 0 TEST_ reports remain). No broad regression run, no product code changed.

minor.issue: Documents an optional CORS_ORIGINS variable that server.py never reads (CORS uses allow_origin_regex='.*'). Either implement it or drop the comment to avoid misleading local users.

62 files on disk vs 8 report + document rows in Mongo — orphaned upload blobs accumulated from earlier iterations (no storage cleanup path). Pre-existing, not caused by this iteration; my test file was removed.

action_items: Optional: remove or implement the CORS_ORIGINS hint in backend/.env.example.

critical_code_review_comments: _require_env correctly treats empty-string values as missing and is evaluated at import time, so misconfiguration fails fast with a clear message — good.
AUTH_SECRET is now required at import; make sure any deploy pipeline that previously relied on a default sets it, otherwise startup will fail (intended fail-fast behaviour).
server.py is ~350 dense one-liner lines; consider splitting routers (auth/availability/reports) for maintainability — not part of this infra fix.
